title.en: What an insurer can read after a run: the log, its limits pack, and incident reports

goal.en: After a run ends, the log names the device, firmware and the exact safety-limits pack that was in force, lists safety events, and marks each step's envelope check. Incidents are reported separately and anonymously.

note.en: Start a shakshuka run with a person present.
The arm cuts; the run waits for a person.
The run is stopped by the operator.
The log: device vendor, model and firmware, the limits pack by id and version, no safety events, every step with envelopeOk true, and the recipe hash that was cooked.
An incident, had there been one, goes to the catalog as an anonymous report; here the example report.

outcome.en: You know which fields of a log an actuarial model can rely on and that incidents are a separate, anonymous stream. Next: scenario 054 covers signatures.
